title: map view: without WebGL2 the map page crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'destroy')" instead of showing its own "Map failed to load" fallback
body:
**Filing gate ① — product defect with a named location and a reproduction.** reach: showcase *Work Map* page (`/apps/com.example.showcase/page/showcase_task_map`) in a browser without WebGL2 (here headless Chromium; also GPU-blocklisted browsers, hardware acceleration off, some VDI/remote desktops).

**Who acts on it:** objectui triage → the console / records owner. ⛔ Not a claim. Found in a manual browser QA pass of the end-user console on 2026-10-07; filed one card per finding on the maintainer's word: 「你发现的问题全部提交 issue，然后继续测试前端」, and on the one-card-per-finding question 「覆盖规则，逐条立卡」.

## What happens

The page body is replaced by the render-failure card: *Component "object-map" failed to render — Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'destroy')* with *Retry*. The message names neither the map nor the real cause. Console sequence on one load:
1. maplibre `GPUInitializationError: WebGL2 is required to display this map …` from `_setupPainter` — the map object is constructed without a painter.
2. 40× `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')` from `map.project` → `locationToScreenPoint`, called by the `<Marker>` children on the painter-less map.
3. The error boundary unmounts the map; react-map-gl's cleanup calls `map.remove()`, which throws `… (reading 'destroy')` — the error the card finally shows.

## Where it comes from (read in source)

`ObjectMap.tsx` (plugin-map) already has the right fallback: `handleMapError` stores the message and the map renders an amber alert "Map failed to load (…). Markers below are still listed in the search box". Maplibre 6.4 reports the missing WebGL2 through that same `error` event, but the markers keep rendering against the map, so the component crashes before the alert can show.

## Expected

Without WebGL2 the view shows its own fallback — the alert plus the record list/search — and the page stays usable; no crash card.

## Suggested direction (triage to rule)

Probe `canvas.getContext('webgl2')` before mounting `MapGL` (or treat an `error` whose name is `GPUInitializationError` as fatal) and, in that state, render the record list instead of `MapGL` and its `Marker`/`Popup` children; a jsdom test with `getContext` returning null pins it.

## Environment

objectstack `879bd38c` · `examples/app-showcase` booted with `objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin` on an isolated port and SQLite file · objectui `179f6fe9` (HEAD; the framework pin `.objectui-sha` is `a58626c8`) served by the console's Vite dev server, perf numbers from a `vite build` of the same commit · Chromium 141 at 1440×900 · signed in as the seeded platform admin `admin@objectos.ai` unless stated.

## Duplicate check

- Semantic issue search on objectstack-ai/objectui (open and closed), *object map WebGL2 not supported GPUInitializationError crash fallback cannot read destroy*: 1 hits (0 open, 1 closed).
- Semantic issue search on objectstack-ai/objectui (open and closed), *ObjectMap markers crash map failed to load banner never shown*: 6 hits (0 open, 6 closed).
- No hit describes this defect.
- Positive control in the same run: *related lists action id refusal notice shown to end users* on objectstack-ai/objectui returned objectstack-ai/objectui#11768: yes.

Dedupe words: object map webgl2 unavailable crash · GPUInitializationError fallback · map.remove destroy undefined error boundary
